system: You are a meticulous senior equity research editor. You audit news summaries written for analysts. You are strict about factual accuracy and you do not reward length.
prompt:
An analyst covering Apple (AAPL) will read the SUMMARY instead of the ARTICLE.
Evaluate the SUMMARY against the ARTICLE only (do not use outside knowledge to fill gaps).

<article>
HEADLINE: Market Chatter: Apple Antitrust Probe in India to Continue Despite Delays

BODY:
07:37 AM EST, 01/15/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Apple (AAPL) has been warned by India that it will continue with an antitrust case against the company by the end of next week if the US tech giant fails to respond to officials investigating its App store, Reuters reported Thursday, citing a confidential Dec. 31 document.

Apple is being accused of attempting to undermine the investigation by delaying responses to the inquiry, the report said.

The commission said Apple has filed numerous requests for extensions since October 2024 instead of answering the allegations, the report said.

Apple has said it could be fined as much as $38 billion in the Competition Commission of India case alleging that abused its monopoly position on its App store, the report said.

Apple did not immediately reply to MT Newswires' request for comment.

(Market Chatter news is derived from conversations with market professionals globally. This information is believed to be from reliable sources but may include rumor and speculation. Accuracy is not guaranteed.)
</article>

<summary>
India's Competition Commission is moving forward with its antitrust probe into Apple's App Store practices, warning it will proceed by the end of next week regardless of the company's response. Regulators allege Apple has repeatedly sought extensions since October 2024 rather than addressing accusations that it abused its monopoly position on the App Store. Apple has previously disclosed potential exposure of up to $38 billion in fines if found liable. The company has not commented on the report. Investors should monitor this case for potential financial and regulatory risk, as it adds to Apple's growing list of global antitrust challenges affecting App Store revenue and business practices.
</summary>

  severity: "material" (could change an investment view) or "minor" (no investment impact)
Step 2 - Omissions. List the most important investment-relevant facts about AAPL in the article that
the summary misses (at most 3).
Step 3 - Score each criterion from 1 to 5:

faithfulness
  5 every claim supported | 4 minor imprecision with no investment impact | 3 one unsupported or distorted claim
  2 several unsupported claims, or one material error (number, direction, company) | 1 largely unsupported

  1 ignores AAPL, or implies the article is about / important for AAPL when it is not
coverage  (key investment-relevant facts: the event, key figures, attribution)
  5 all key facts | 3 misses some important facts | 1 misses the main point
conciseness
  5 no filler, easy to scan | 3 some redundancy or filler | 1 verbose or hard to parse
